behavior: Contract v1 fixes from the attacker and stuck-funds review plus invoice status views: every payable address stays deployable, holds are capped, recover works with broken invoice tokens, deploy is restricted to our keys, and status can be read by invoice id
acceptance: predict and deploy never reject terms (an address that can hold money is always deployable); settle refuses amount 0, chain mismatch and a recipient that is 0, the receiver, the factory, the implementation or the token, so such money goes to refund instead
The executor-to-authority switch and full refunds open at min(settleDeadline, deployedAt + 30 days), so wrong or huge deadlines cannot freeze money

recover reads the invoice-token balance with a low-level call: a token without code or with a reverting balanceOf no longer blocks recovery of other tokens or the native coin; the Arc native-USDC guard still holds

deploy is callable only by the executor or the refund authority, records deployedAt and receiverOf(invoiceId) (first write wins); factory.status(terms), factory.statusOf(invoiceId) and receiver.status() return receiver, deployed, chain match, balance, settled, refundable, settleable and who may settle now; Settled, Refunded and Recovered events carry invoiceId

packages/contracts/AGENTS.md, PLAN.md and the diagrams describe these rules and the new process rules (Guard checks the Delay inner operation and txExpiration, independent canary, pause alert, Arc checkout uses ERC-20 transfer and balanceOf, testnet keys never shown to real payers, Safe original owner keys kept recoverable); tests cover every change
notes: 2026-10-08 review fail by reviewer: FAIL (1 must-fix, acceptance 4). forge test 65 pass/1 skip, fmt ok; Fork test pass; halmos 3/3 pass. MUST FIX: InvoiceReceiverFactory.sol:101 settleable ignores the new settle term checks (InvoiceReceiver.sol:87-90: recipient 0/receiver/factory/implementation/token). PoC: terms with recipient=0, paid AMOUNT, deployed -> status().settleable==true, settle() by status().settler reverts InvalidTerms. So status lies exactly for the unsafe-terms invoices this change makes deployable (money that must go to refund is reported as ready to settle), contradicting the InvoiceStatus comment (InvoiceTypes.sol:24) and the claim in Status.t.sol testFuzz_statusMatchesBehaviour, which only fuzzes valid terms. Fix: move the term checks into one pure function in InvoiceTypes.sol (like refundableAmount), e.g. safeTerms(t, receiver, factory, implementation), use it in settle and in _status (receiver = s.receiver, factory = address(this), implementation), and add the bad-recipient/amount-0 cases to the status test. No money moved by this bug. CHECKED OK: no-validation deploy (amount 0, recipient bad, token 0, chainId 0, deadline 0 or uint64 max) never strands money: settle refuses, refund/recover return it (PoCs incl. token=0 native recover on intended chain); deployedAt+MAX_HOLD cannot overflow; cap only moves settle/full refund to the refund authority, never to anyone else; executor deploys at settle time per backend rule so long (<=365d) invoices settle normally; tryBalanceOf ok for no code, reverting, short (<32 bytes) data and gas-burning balanceOf (recover passes with 10M gas); Arc native guard test still passes; status/statusOf views are staticcalls, no reentrancy; deploy restriction: authority can deploy and replace executor, Smoke/deploy.sh use the executor key. RESIDUAL (not blocking, compromised API/evil invoice token only, not a regression): an invoice token that mirrors another token's balance, or returns ~3MB (return bomb, tryBalanceOf copies all returndata, InvoiceTypes.sol:58), makes recover of other tokens revert permanently on the intended chain; optional hardening: read only 32 bytes of returndata in assembly. statusOf hides a second receiver with a duplicate invoiceId (documented). FOLLOW-UP: deployments.json lists the F037 factory built from old bytecode (permissionless deploy, term validation); the new code needs a new factory address and redeploy task.
